companies.name: Simantic
companies.oneLiner: Firmware simulation for AI agents
companies.longDescription: Simantic is modernizing the embedded firmware industry with hardware simulation developed for the adoption of AI in hardware engineering. Simantic gives both humans and AI the visibility into hardware previously limited by the physical world.

companies.name: Experiential Labs
companies.oneLiner: World models for agents
companies.longDescription: An applied AI research lab building world models for agents. We simulate reality faster and more accurately based on the technology self-driving uses to get 99.7% reconstruction fidelity.

companies.name: Edviro
companies.oneLiner: Energy world models that fix energy waste before it becomes expensive.
companies.longDescription:
Edviro helps facilities managers at large buildings save on their energy bills. Facilities managers are overwhelmed with dashboards, alarms, and analytics for hundreds of boilers, HVAC units, and heat pumps across their buildings. Edviro continuously monitors and optimizes buildings using energy world models to detect anomalies, simulate interventions, and suggest the best options to the facilities manager.  Once the changes occur, we create a comprehensive M&V report to ensure savings show up on the bill. 

Our tools also allow institutions to maintain detailed service history & equipment logs, and perform maintenance with AR.

companies.name: Coasty
companies.oneLiner: Building the future of knowledge work, RPA and SOPs using computer use
companies.longDescription:
Coasty is a computer use agent that does real work inside softwares, companies already run. New web apps, old desktop tools, the legacy systems nobody wants to touch. You hand it a workflow and it owns the outcome.
Most agents demo well and break the moment they hit real software. They get 18 steps out of 20 right, misclick once, and everything after is garbage. Coasty catches when it goes off track and fixes itself mid-task instead of starting over. It handles the messy parts, benchmarks never show. Permission dialogs, surprise pop-ups, a modal that steals focus, a page that loads slow. When a vendor pushes an overnight update and moves half the menus, brittle scripts break by morning. Coasty reads the screen instead of recording clicks, so it adapts and keeps going.
It also checks its own output and leaves a time-stamped trail you can replay. We won't pretend it gets every task right. Nothing automating this work does. What matters is what happens when something breaks. It catches the mistake, fixes what it can, and flags what it can't so a person can step in. Nothing fails quietly. That's what lets a team trust it on the work where a silent error gets someone fired.
We scored 82% on OSWorld, which puts us among the most reliable agents out there. Reliability is the whole product, not a feature.

companies.name: Salem Robotics Inc
companies.oneLiner: We deploy robots for inspections in hazardous spaces, like nuclear.
companies.longDescription: Our software turns any robot we deploy into an everyday independent worker at your facility. They are able to walk sites, handle instruments, overcome obstacles, collect measurements, and generate auditable compliance records, replacing hours of manual surveys and inspections. Built by Los Alamos robotics veterans and deterministic-manipulation researchers, we're starting in nuclear and expanding to other hazardous industries.

companies.name: Justinian
companies.oneLiner: Builders of the first AI-native government affairs firm.
companies.longDescription:
Justinian is an applied AI company changing the way companies and governments work together. 

Our first focus is building Justinian Government Affairs, an AI-native government affairs firm helping early-stage companies monitor regulations, lobby policymakers, and win government contracts.

companies.name: Florin
companies.oneLiner: The financial operating system for the companies building the future.
companies.longDescription: Florin brings banking, payments, cards, and treasury into one account built for startups - so founders can hold, move, and grow their capital without stitching together half a dozen tools. Unlike platforms that resell another bank's rails, we're building the infrastructure ourselves, end to end, so money moves in real time on a single ledger we own. We start with an invite-only membership for venture-backed companies and expand from there. Named after the florin, the coin that anchored global trade for three centuries, with infrastructure built for how money moves now.

companies.name: Hop Aero
companies.oneLiner: Rocket cargo delivery to contested environments
companies.longDescription: Hop Aero is building rocket cargo vehicles that deliver to contested environments hundreds of miles away in minutes. Our rockets fly point-to-point into the most austere locations at hypersonic speeds. Hop Aero's goal is to provide the U.S. and allies the asymmetric advantage that deters a future major conflict.

companies.name: Mireye
companies.oneLiner: Infrastructure for Physical World AI Agents
companies.longDescription:
AI agents are starting to act in the real world, but they can't reliably understand it. 

Geospatial data is complex, fragmented, and unstructured. Ask a model a specific question about a specific place and it guesses. Our API and MCP give agents cited answers about any location.

Our mission is to index every inch of the earth, and make it as queryable as the web.

companies.name: Levocred AI
companies.oneLiner: AI for every workflow inside a credit team
companies.longDescription: Levocred AI is the Company Brain for credit teams — an AI employee that plugs into the fund's loan tape, credit agreements, servicer reports, and bank feeds, and runs the workflows analysts would otherwise grind on.

companies.name: Praxis AI
companies.oneLiner: Turns every company into a data vendor
companies.longDescription: Praxis captures the data physical AI is bottlenecked on: egocentric video, 3D scans, and multimodal capture from inside real industrial and residential environments. Embedded within publicly listed and unicorn-scale conglomerates, we reach 60k workers across 5 continents and 150+ environment types, supplying the real-world training data frontier labs and humanoid companies can't source anywhere else.

companies.name: Care GP
companies.oneLiner: AI agents to run primary healthcare operations
companies.longDescription: Care GP is building AI agents to run operations for primary healthcare clinics

companies.name: Agentcard
companies.oneLiner: debit cards for AI agents.
companies.longDescription: Agentcard.sh is a debit card for AI agents. Agents can use Agentcard’s API to issue cards and pay for things online autonomously.

companies.name: Inkbox
companies.oneLiner: Give your AI agents email, phone, iMessage and an internet address
companies.longDescription: We are building the identity and communication layer for AI agents: giving agents their own email, phone, iMessage, and internet address. Every interaction flows through Inkbox, so agents are enhanced with multi-channel context.

companies.name: Operon
companies.oneLiner: Agentic data layer for manufacturing & process industries.
companies.longDescription:
Operon is the data intelligence layer for heavy industry. We ingest the messy documents a plant runs on (P&IDs, schematics, datasheets, scans) and turn them into one structured, queryable model of the facility.

On top of it, engineers query their plant in natural language and build agentic workflows for safety, compliance, and design.

companies.name: Cosmic Robotics
companies.oneLiner: Autonomous construction on Earth and beyond
companies.longDescription:
Our mission is to build a city on Mars. 

Cosmic-1, the first equipment in our fleet, is an autonomous robot capable of heavy-lift manipulation. Its been deployed on some of the largest solar farms in the US, more than doubling labor productivity across tens of thousands of panel installs. 

We're scaling in solar, expanding in data centers, and building lunar construction robotics under contract with NASA.

companies.name: Markov
companies.oneLiner: Data for computer-use ai
companies.longDescription: We source high quality tasks and data to train the next generation of computer use AI models.

companies.name: Denta
companies.oneLiner: The dental practice that runs itself
companies.longDescription:
Denta is the practice management platform that puts dental practices on autopilot. When a dentist starts a new practice, instead of finding an accounting firm, hiring two front desk workers, and then spending their nights posting insurance payments, they use Denta.

I started Denta to help operate my Dad's 10 practices in Iowa. In supporting those, I realized the most painful part was both people and agents having messy access to fragmented data. So I solved for that and now spend my time automating work for dentists!

companies.name: Isengard Industries Inc
companies.oneLiner: Mass-produced AI strike systems and Counter-UAS
companies.longDescription:
Isengard Industries is not another drone company.

We build sovereign production: the means for allied nations to make precision-strike and counter-drone systems by the thousand, on their own soil, at a fraction of what the primes charge.

We call it Weapons of Mass Production. The Arsenal of Democracy, rebuilt for the drone age.

More to come, and only where it helps. You know how to reach us.

companies.name: LATO
companies.oneLiner: Agent-native research and simulation platform for investors
companies.longDescription:
The best investments come from conviction, and conviction comes from understanding a market deeply: its customers, its competitors, and where it's heading.

Today that understanding is slow and expensive to build. Reaching the right people takes weeks, a commercial study costs $300k+, and each one starts from scratch.

LATO does this research end-to-end, combining public data and the fund's own knowledge with first-hand interviews of a market's customers, experts, and operators. This research grounds a simulation of the market to predict how market participants behave.

companies.name: Risklytics
companies.oneLiner: AI-powered catastrophe risk modeling
companies.longDescription: We build AI-powered catastrophe risk models that help insurers, reinsurers, and financial institutions better understand and quantify natural disaster risk. Our platform combines continuously updated data, property-level analysis, and synthetic catastrophe simulations to deliver more accurate, transparent, and flexible risk assessments than traditional catastrophe models.

companies.name: Whitespace
companies.oneLiner: AI Operating System for Wholesale Distributors
companies.longDescription: Whitespace is the AI operating system for wholesale distributors. It connects to their systems and inboxes to build a living model of their business, then deploys self-improving AI agents to automate work like inventory planning, customer support, and order entry.

companies.name: Greypoint Industries
companies.oneLiner: Manufacturing the future of autonomous swarm warfare.
companies.longDescription: Greypoint Industries builds mass-produced autonomous interceptors that defeat drone saturation for a fraction of the cost of the targets. We are developing a soldier-deployable, fire-and-forget interceptor built to give Western and allied forces the ammunition to counter mass drone swarm attacks.
